title: Equivariant regularization of the constants of a normal alteration
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and $b:S\to Y$ an alteration. Let $H$ be a finite group acting compatibly on $k,Y$, let $J$ be a finite group with a surjection $\rho:J\to H$, and let $J$ act on $S$ compatibly with $b$ and the induced action on $k$. Write $A=\ker\rho$ and suppose that $k(S)^A/k(Y)$ is purely inseparable. There exist a finite extension $e/k$ with a $J$-action extending the action on $k$, a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $e$-scheme $B$ with compatible $J$-action, and a $J$-equivariant finite surjective radicial morphism $q:B\to S$. Radicial means universally injective. The extension $k(B)/k(S)$ is finite purely inseparable, $k(B)^A/k(Y)$ is purely inseparable, and $e^A/k$ is purely inseparable. The structural inclusion $e\hookrightarrow k(B)$ identifies $e$ with the algebraic closure of $k$ in $k(B)$. The composite $B\to Y$ is H-projective. If $\dim Y=0$, then $B=\operatorname{Spec}e$.

Field, integral scheme, proper morphism, finite type, geometric integrality, projectivity, finite morphism, surjectivity, function field and field extensions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target; it does not refer to a group named H. A normal scheme has integrally closed domains as local rings. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes, finite over a dense open of the target. A purely inseparable extension in characteristic p>0 means that every element has some p-power in the smaller field; in characteristic zero it means equality. All group actions below are by scheme or field automorphisms, and are allowed to be nonfaithful.

source.place: de Jong (1997), Lemma 5.5 and proof, printed p.614, applied over Spec k: purely inseparable geometric reduction and Stein constants. Geometric-normal preparation is Stacks Tag 0BXT (varieties-lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-normal); the fixed-field conclusion uses the geometric integrality of Y. proof.text: By [lem-sfb-normal-inseparable-normalization-radicial], normality of $S$ makes this $q$ finite surjective radicial, and $F/K$ finite purely inseparable, where $F=k(B)$ and $K=k(S)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-projective-stein-constants] to the finite $q$ over projective $S$. It gives $e=\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)$, the finite algebraic constant field in $F$, its compatible $J$-action, and a projective proper map $B\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ with geometrically connected fibres. It also gives finite $e/l$ and H-projectivity of $bq$, since $Y/k$ is separated.

proof.text: Over $l$, $B$ is proper and geometrically normal; over its global-section field $e$ its canonical map is proper with geometrically connected fibres. Thus [lem-sfb-geonormal-stein-geometric-integrality] makes $B/e$ geometrically integral. This supplies all geometric and constant-field identification clauses.

proof.text: For $Y$, projectivity implies properness. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-stein-constant-field] over $k$ and [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety](2): $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=k$, so $k$ is algebraically closed in $L=k(Y)$.

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $x\in F^A$, pure inseparability gives $x^{p^n}\in K$, hence in $K^A$, and then $x^{p^{n+m}}\in L$ by the hypothesis on $K^A/L$. For $c\in e^A$, the resulting $c^{p^r}\in L$ is algebraic over $k$, so belongs to $k$ by step 5. Thus $F^A/L$ and $e^A/k$ are purely inseparable. In characteristic zero $F=K$ and $K^A=L$, while $e^A\subseteq L$ is algebraic over $k$, giving $e^A=k$. These are extensions since $A$ fixes $k$ and $L$, by compatibility through $\rho$.

proof.text: If $\dim Y=0$, [lem-pc-algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite] makes $Y$ affine finite over $k$, and [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety](2) gives $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its only dense open is itself, so the alteration $b$ is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b), $B$ is affine. Its canonical map identifies $B=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)=\operatorname{Spec}e$, equivariantly.
